text:
maria: Heads up — finance pinged me about a surprise increase in committed pool charges for Dedicated customers in us-west-2. Looks like line items for 'Reserved GPU - dedicated' jumped compared to our forecast. Can infra folks triage?

ajay: On it. Do we have the exact invoice lines / ARNs? I can run a Cost Explorer slice.

maria: finance-bot dropped the invoice snippet earlier, attaching key lines: 
finance-bot: Invoice 2026-02 - us-west-2: ReservedGPUCharges = $162,400; Forecasted = $128,900; Delta = $33,500 (26%).

kevin: Two quick hypotheses: 1) mis-sized reserved pool (too many GPUs reserved), or 2) burst billing (we hit reserved+on-demand transition due to autoscale config).

ellie: Also check if any recent region failovers pushed traffic into us-west-2 — that would increase effective utilization of reserved capacity and show as over-commit?

ajay: Running a Cost Explorer query now, will post the query and results.
ajay: Query snippet: ```aws ce get-cost-and-usage --time-period Start=2026-02-01,End=2026-02-28 --granularity MONTHLY --filter '{"Dimensions":{"Key":"REGION","Values":["us-west-2"]}}' --metrics "UnblendedCost" "UsageQuantity"```

deploy-bot: reserved-pool-alert: us-west-2/dedicated-pool-3 utilization = 92% peak (2026-02-18T14:22Z) ; autoscale bumped 8 extra on-demand GPUs for 3h.

sophia: 92% peak + 3h of on-demand could explain ~20-30k delta depending on GPU SKU. Which SKU? A100 or H100?

maria: It's mixed. Dedicated pool 3 is mostly A100-80GB but we started onboarding H100s in late Jan and a few jobs pinned to H100 in that pool. Cost per-hour ratio caused the spike.

kevin: Quick sizing calc I ran last week: required GPUs = ceil(peak_tokens_per_sec / per_gpu_tokens). Example: peak_tokens = 1.2M tokens/s, per A100 = ~8k tokens/s (gen 13B quant), so GPUs = ceil(1200000/8000)=150. If we reserved 200 we would obviously be overpaying.

ellie: Where do the 200 reserved number come from? Was that an old on-prem sizing carryover?

ajay: I pulled commit configuration: us-west-2:dedi-pool-3 = 220 committed GPUs (monthly contract). Live autoscale target = 140. So commit >> steady-state usage.

sophia: That mismatch is the likely root cause. Committing to 220 when steady is ~140 => ~80 GPUs idle being billed.

maria: Did we commit before major customer wins? Might be a contract from Q4 expecting growth that didn't materialize.

finance-bot: Contract: Dedicated Commit Q4-2025 — committed GPUs: 220 across us-west-2; start 2026-01-01; term 12 months; monthly charge = $X (redacted).

kevin: Action items: 1) Verify if contract allows rebalancing or regional transfer of commits. 2) Measure actual 7/30/90-day avg GPUs in use (by SKU and by time-of-day). 3) Propose a sliding commit (e.g., 150 base + 60 burst) or smaller committed floor + burst pool.

ajay: I can run the usage aggregation. Quick BQ snippet I used before: ```SELECT sku, HOUR(ts) as hr, AVG(gpu_count) AS avg_gpu FROM `billing.dedicated_usage` WHERE region='us-west-2' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2026-02-28' GROUP BY sku, hr;```

ellie: If contract can't change, we should consider moving lower-cost H100 workloads to a different pool/region and scavenge burst to spot or preemptible where SLA allows.
sophia: Also check per-customer pinning — a couple of enterprise customers pinned to pool-3 for data isolation. Maybe we can split them into a smaller committed pool and a 'shared burst' pool.

maria: Good. For the immediate short term (this week) can we: reduce autoscale min, throttle scheduled large training jobs to non-peak hours, and open a finance support ticket for rate reconciliation?

ajay: I reduced autoscale min from 120 -> 80 for pool-3 (will monitor). If we see evictions or customer impact I'll rollback.

deploy-bot: config-change: autoscale-min updated for us-west-2/dedicated-pool-3 by ajay at 2026-03-05T09:12Z.

kevin: I'll draft a proposal for re-tiering the commit: 150 committed A100s + 40 dedicated H100s + 30 buffer (burst) and show delta vs current monthly charge.
sophia: I'll inventory which customers are pinned to pool-3 and propose migration windows.

maria: Thanks. Can we aim for a short runbook for finance explaining the delta and a 2-week mitigation plan? We'll need it for the account team.

ellie: I can draft the runbook today. Outline: root cause, evidence (cost query + deploy-bot peaks), mitigations (autoscale/min reduction, job throttling, customer migration), and longer-term options (contract rebalancing or sliding commit).

kevin: Estimated savings if we move to 150 commit: ~ $27k/month (rough estimate). I'll refine once BQ results land.

ajay: Posting full Cost Explorer export to the shared drive now (/mnt/reports/usw2-dedicated-2026-02.csv).

maria: Perfect. Keep this thread for updates. If anyone sees customer errors, ping #support immediately. :thumbsup:
